# Combined review of D1/P1

Verdict: **needs changes**. Open finding: **R1**. Next action: make P1's implementation and verification prerequisites explicit, then recheck P1. D1 has no material static-review findings against REQUEST.md.

## Scope and evidence

Reviewed the supplied candidate snapshot, baseline commit `a6b1a861a7ff7f3b461d920db0e59a988ec46c87`: `docs/DESIGN.md` (Design D1) and `docs/PLAN.md` (Plan P1), against `REQUEST.md` and fixture `AGENTS.md`. Applied the review operations and shared artifact contracts in `skills/feature-design` and `skills/implementation-plan`.

This is an independent document review in a fresh context, separate from artifact authorship. It is not independent implementation review, executed validation, or human acceptance. Static inspection covered the supplied documents and the fixture file inventory, including hidden-file discovery excluding Git internals. No application code, API definitions, tests, check configuration, additional review policy, or prior reports were found. Repository compatibility and implementation feasibility therefore remain unverified. No tests were run and no implementation was started. Reviewed artifacts were left unchanged; this report is new. Git returned the baseline identifier, with sandbox cache/config-access warnings; those warnings provide no validation evidence.

## Assessment

D1's private stock copy addresses caller-input preservation. Preflight before any debit addresses all-or-nothing reservation. Its example correctly rejects `a=1,b=1` against `a=2,b=0` without changing stock, then accepts a later batch requesting `a=2`. The single-process, in-memory boundary matches REQUEST.md. Static reasoning supports this approach; runtime correctness is not established.

P1's single increment is proportionate to this local change. Its proposed acceptance covers the decisive rejected multi-item batch followed by a valid batch and caller-input preservation. Separate stages, extra documents, and an alternatives catalog are unnecessary. Its proposed status correctly avoids claiming execution. The unresolved issue is the unavailable basis for compatibility and the completion gate.

## R1 — High priority — Open

**Location:** `docs/PLAN.md:2`, “API-compatible,” “existing API checks,” and “The established gate and independent review apply before committing.”

**Trigger and evidence:** An implementer following P1 in this fixture cannot locate the API, existing checks, gate command/configuration, or the referenced review policy. `AGENTS.md` supplies operating restrictions, including no commits, but defines no test gate. No corresponding source or configuration is present in the supplied file inventory.

**Consequence:** The implementer cannot establish API compatibility or determine what evidence satisfies completion. Treating the referenced checks as available would invent repository facts. This document review cannot satisfy a future implementation-review requirement.

**Minimal correction:** Identify the missing implementation repository/API and verification configuration as prerequisites, and make implementation readiness conditional on inspecting them. If the intended gate and review policy are actually available, cite their concrete source and applicable commands. Otherwise explicitly mark them unresolved rather than “established”; distinguish proposed checks from available checks and retain the current no-commit restriction. No new tooling or implementation is required to correct the plan.

**Verification:** Statically recheck the revised plan: every claimed existing gate/API check must resolve to supplied evidence, or be explicitly pending with a clear prerequisite before implementation. Once the implementation fixture is supplied in a separately authorized phase, verify compatibility, check discovery and the applicable review gate there. No tests are required for this document recheck.

Goal: resolve material uncertainty and leave an implementable decision. Select one operation; load its linked contract/example when needed and its self-check after generation.

Choose depth by uncertainty, failure consequences/reversibility and affected interfaces/owners, not a difficulty score. description: Turn a feature design into reviewable stage and commit boundaries, or review that plan for dependencies, acceptance criteria, and feasibility. Use for implementation planning rather than executing code changes.

# Implementation plan

Goal: make the next coherent outcome, dependencies and acceptance usable without maintaining another implementation in prose.

Select [Plan implementation](prompts/plan-implementation.md) to write/revise, or [Review implementation plan](prompts/review-implementation.md) to review. Each loads the same substantive plan contract and an after-generation check when needed.

Ground work in original requirements, confirmed decisions and current code. A sufficient local design/plan note is valid input; do not invent extra documents or approval steps. Preserve the chosen task depth and actual review policy. Expand stages for delivery, dependency, risk or ownership boundaries, not components or test counts.

Templates are adaptable examples; repository conventions take precedence. Default artifacts to English and resolve resources within this bundle. Planning does not implement or commit; unexecuted work remains proposed.
# Review the design

Read original requirements, confirmed clarifications, relevant code and the exact design version. Assess the shared [design contract](../assets/design.template.md), including a combined design/plan note when appropriate. Use the [review feedback contract and example](../assets/review.template.md) to report findings; review does not edit the design or product.

Judge concrete behavior, consequences and usability at the selected task depth. Accept sufficient work. A separate document, alternatives catalog or stylistic preference is not a prerequisite. Do not enlarge the task to satisfy the example. If independent review was requested, use a genuinely separate authorized context when available; otherwise disclose self-review.

On recheck, compare the relevant revision and evidence before revisiting findings. An unchanged verified resolution can be cited while it remains applicable. A changed contract, new evidence or incomplete prior verification requires checking the whole affected invariant; do not reopen unrelated decisions. Perform explicitly required rechecks even when content is unchanged.

After writing feedback, load the Review section of [artifact checks](../references/artifact-checks.md). Correct supported reporting defects without generating a self-review report or another round. Disclose unresolved issues.
# Review the implementation plan

Read the source requirements, confirmed design, exact plan version, relevant code and actual check configuration. Assess the shared [plan contract](../assets/implementation-plan.template.md), then use the [review feedback contract and example](../assets/review.template.md). Do not edit the plan or implementation during review. Disclose whether the review is independent or self-review.

Check delivery order, dependency/boundary reasons, acceptance and feasibility against the current repository. Planned commands must be distinguished from available ones; zero collected tests cannot establish success. A short combined note or single increment can be sufficient. Block for a concrete contract, dependency, risk or usability consequence, not preferred headings, test counts or separate documents.

On recheck, compare the relevant revision and evidence. Cite an unchanged verified resolution while it remains applicable; changed assumptions/content or missing verification require checking the full affected contract. Honor required rechecks and preserve original findings. Do not reopen unrelated completed decisions or continue cosmetic cycles.

After writing feedback, load the Review section of [artifact checks](../references/artifact-checks.md). Correct supported reporting defects; disclose unresolved issues without a new self-review report or round.
